g.text: dashed outlines are the originals; each level adds its own loss term

svg.text: Read 1. Every word enters as a vector.
Attention runs over the word sequence, then argmax pooling merges each group into one sentence vector.
The same step one level up: attention over sentences, pooled into paragraphs.
Chapters are pooled into a single vector: the document representation.
Read 2. The book vector is appended to every word, so attention at each level can see the whole book.
Each pooled vector, from book down to sentence, is placed in the latent space.
Genre, scores and reviews can further constrain the latent space.
A glyph module draws the symbol stroke by stroke, constrained by a prescribed stroke topology.
Every level gets its own glyph: chapters, paragraphs and sentences too.
Soft interpolation noise is applied to the glyphs before decoding.
Decoding starts from the glyph alone.
The decoder rebuilds the book vector, and the demultiplexer splits it back down the hierarchy.
Each rebuilt level is compared with its original. Together these losses push the glyph to hold as much of the book as possible.
